title: Unchecked nil dereference of speaker device config
disposition: Repaired in final source, with focused electrical/codec/desktop regressions.

title: Speaker schema property paths may not match nested parameters
disposition: The helper annotates SpeakerConfig itself in SchemaRegistry, not SpeakerParams. The command parameters property references urn:elab:speaker-config:1. Tests inspect that reference and every referenced bound/unit; no missing annotation was reproduced.

title: Speaker dissipation not included in total power
disposition: Private R primitives add their heat before the private/public filter; private L/C add instantaneous storage power but are omitted from public storage arrays. The speaker parent is a summary. Tests assert empty public private-storage arrays, exact scope energy equal to the one speaker summary, independent ODE/AC laws and strict power residual. Generic transistor JunctionEnergy is exactly zero; profiled devices trigger the reset/sum path and have independent scope-energy regression.

title: Test silently passes on budget refusal
disposition: This is deliberately a separate high-complexity atomic-refusal regression, not a waveform test. Independent positive speaker transient tests require 50 successful advances against an ODE; the powered-follower example completes capture/audio/round trips. title: Possible nil dereference of Device.Speaker during lowering
disposition: Graph.Compile validates explicit device parameters before lowering. Saved/recorded graphs go through the same admission; a dedicated missing-config test proves refusal before this private helper. No valid public route supplies an unvalidated component.

title: decimalControlSI returns NaN which is forwarded to commands
disposition: Intentional invalid-entry refusal: encoding/json refuses NaN before service Dispatch; device validators also require finite values. It cannot enter accepted physics. Ordinary finite UI minima/maxima are separately tested with exact decimal SI conversion.

title: Preview normalization amplifies near-floor residue to full gain
disposition: Peak normalization is an explicitly labeled waveform illustration, not acoustic loudness. A 1 microvolt raw-signal floor suppresses numerical residue, with tests for residue silence, DC filter priming, meaningful normalized PCM and gain bounds. No calibrated SPL or electrical noise-floor claim.

title: Duplicated speaker/sound kind predicate
disposition: Small explicit symbol/terminal/label cases are retained; the full new-kind drawing and descriptor tests cover their consistency. No demonstrated defect warrants widening legacy sound-kind contracts.

title: Speaker restore runs before other node restores it depends on
disposition: Speaker terminals are authored public nets, populated from result.Nodes before any private restore. Later restores modify only reserved private nodes; callers cannot connect authored terminals to those generated nodes. Missing private-node guards are explicit.

title: Fake audio player state read without synchronization
disposition: Render never calls the player. Fake Play/data writes happen synchronously through guarded service commands before the test reads them; asynchronous stop only changes its distinct stop counter. Race tests pass. No hardware audibility is claimed.

title: Uninformative failure when capability count is wrong
disposition: Low test-diagnostic observation only; explicit companion discovery regression reports count and error and verifies the referenced schema. No product defect.
